newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila money mkt quiet ahead of short bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Manila money mkt quiet ahead of short bill auction.

text.p: Lacklustre trading marked the Philippine money market on Tuesday as traders focused on investing in the special short-term Treasury bill auction in the afternoon, traders said.
"Everybody's looking forward to the 35-day and 45-day T-bill auction. They're expecting good rates on the bills," one trader at a large commercial bank said.
Traders were expecting yields of 16.0 to 18.0 percent for the special bills which are specially offered to beef up government's cash position.
The Bureau of Treasury has been rejecting T-bill bids in recent weeks due to the high interest rates.
"It's better to invest in these special bills rather than buy the regular bills at very low yields," another trader said.
Bid and offer quotes in the secondary T-bill market were wide and disparate because banks were still unsure on the outlook of domestic interest rates.
"It's a confused market. Banks are still waiting for a definite direction on where the rates will go," the second trader said.
On Monday, T-bill rates corrected slightly after several weeks of uptrend due to uncertainties in the foreign exchange market.
"Some banks still believe that rates will remain firm since the regional currencies are still under attack," the trader added.
Bids for the benchmark three-month bills ranged from 13.375 to 14.0 percent, while offers were from 12.5 to 13.5 percent.
The interbank call loan rate slipped to 25.0625 percent from Monday's 25.09375 percent. Turnover slowed to 12.38 billion pesos from 13.94 billion.
